sourceType: Official Rajasthan Tourism website (Government of Rajasthan)
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: Founded 1156 by Rawal Jaisal, eldest heir of the Rawal of Deoraj, passed over for the throne of Lodurva; guided by sage Eesul to the site per a Krishna prophecy of the Yaduvanshi clan. 'Golden City', close to the Pakistan border and the Thar Desert. Wood Fossil Park (Akal) 180-million-year-old fossils 15km away.

places.name: Laser Water Show at Gadisar Lake
places.facts: One of the first/largest laser water shows in India; water-screen projection mapping via 3-chip DLP 25,000-lumen projectors; depicts the founding of Jaisalmer, fort battles, Tanot Mata Temple, Lodruva Temple, Laxminarayan Temple, and Longewala war scenes.

places.name: Jaisalmer Fort (Sonar Quila)
places.facts: 'Golden Fort'; UNESCO World Heritage Site; living fort with shops, hotels, and havelis still inhabited; built by local craftsmen in classic Rajput style; featured in Satyajit Ray's Feluda story/film Sonar Kella.

places.name: Jaisalmer Government Museum
places.facts: Run by the Department of Archaeology and Museums; notable Godawan (Great Indian Bustard, Rajasthan's state bird) trophy display; traditional household items, rock-cut crockery, jewellery, 7th-9th century AD statues.

places.name: Nathmal Ji Ki Haveli
places.facts: Built 19th century by two architect brothers working from opposite sides, resulting in near-symmetrical construction; miniature-style paintings; carved yellow sandstone elephants.

places.name: Salim Singh Ki Haveli
places.facts: Built first half of the 18th century; still partly occupied by descendants; high arched roof supported by peacock-shaped carved brackets; legend says two upper wooden storeys were demolished on the Maharaja's order to keep it shorter than the royal palace.

places.name: Patwon Ki Haveli
places.facts: Among the largest, most elaborately carved havelis in Jaisalmer; five-storey structure; some interior paintings and mirror work survive despite losing some of its original grandeur.

places.name: Mandir Palace (Badal Mahal / Cloud Palace)
places.facts: Five-storey palace with pagoda-like Tazia Tower, built by Muslim craftsmen in the shape of a Muharram procession float (Tazia); intricately carved balconies on each floor.

places.name: Jain Temples of Jaisalmer
places.facts: Date to 12th-15th centuries; dedicated to Tirthankaras Rikhabdevji and Shambhavdevji; carved from yellow sandstone in the Dilwara architectural style.

places.name: Bada Bagh (Barabagh)
places.facts: Garden complex with royal Jaisalmer chhatris (cenotaphs), including that of Jai Singh II; known sunset viewpoint.

places.name: Desert National Park
places.facts: Sand dunes, jagged rocks, salt lake bottoms; blackbuck, chinkara, desert fox; Great Indian Bustard; winter raptor migrants (Himalayan/Eurasian Griffon Vulture, Eastern Imperial Eagle, Saker Falcon).

places.name: Kuldhara
places.facts: Abandoned village, legend says ~85 villages of Paliwal Brahmins vanished overnight in the 1800s fleeing an unscrupulous minister; remains uninhabited and a popular 'mystery' tourist site.

places.name: Tanot Mata Temple
places.facts: Tanot Mata considered a reincarnation of Goddess Hinglaj; folklore holds that shells/bombs fired at the temple during the 1965 India-Pakistan war did not explode; rebuilt post-war and now managed by a BSF Trust.

places.name: Ramdevra Temple
places.location: 12 km from Pokhran, on the Jodhpur-Jaisalmer route
places.facts: Dedicated to saint Baba Ramdevji (commonly mistaken for a Ram temple); marks his resting place; large Ramdevra Fair held Aug-Sept with all-night devotional singing.

places.name: Jaisalmer War Museum
places.facts: Commemorates 1965 war and 1971 Longewala battle; captured tanks, war memorabilia, audio-visual room, interview footage with Major Kuldip Singh Chandpuri (Longewala); IAF Hunter aircraft used in the Battle of Longewala; free entry.

places.name: Longewala War Memorial
places.facts: Commemorates the 4 December 1971 Battle of Longewala where ~100 Indian defenders held off ~2,000 Pakistani soldiers and 60 tanks.

places.name: Akal Wood Fossil Park
places.facts: 21-hectare protected area; 180-million-year-old fossilized tree trunks from a submerged Jurassic-era forest; ~25 fossilized tree specimens under corrugated-iron shelters; visitors can touch a fossilized red-wood trunk near the entrance.

places.name: Vyas Chhatri
places.facts: Old Brahmin cemetery/cenotaph cluster dedicated to sage Ved Vyas (author of the Mahabharata); popular sunset point with golden sandstone carved chhatris; local musicians often play the algoza (double flute) here.

places.name: Amar Sagar Lake
places.facts: Lake-cum-oasis beside the 17th-century Amar Singh Palace; includes ponds, wells, a Shiva temple, and carved stone animal figureheads believed to protect the royal family; a carved Jain temple sits at one end.

howToReach.air: Jaisalmer civil airport, direct connectivity from Jaipur, Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Surat
howToReach.road: Connected to Jodhpur, Bikaner, and Jaipur by bus and taxi
